To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pharmacological isolation of polysynaptic responses is possible in the isolated CA3-CA1 region of the hippocampus.
blocking gamma-aminobuytric acid-A inhibition reveals AMPA and/orNMDA-receptor mediated polysynaptic responses, driven by local recurrent connections in the CA1 hippocampal region.

blocking GABA(A) receptor-mediated inhibition reveals polysynaptic responses, mediated by both NMDA- and AMPA-type glutamate receptors, that are generated via local recurrent collaterates in the CA1 hippocampus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of polysynaptic responses mediated by AMPA or NMDA receptors in the isolated CA3 region of the hippocampus.
the mechanisms underlying polysynaptic responses and their possible role in the generation of epileptic discharges.
the generation of polysynaptic responses and their pharmacology in the isolated CA 1 region of the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polysynapic responses are generated by local recurrent collateral branches of CA3 and/or CA1 pyramical neurons.

the isolated CA1 pyramal cells are able to generate a polysynaptic response in the presence of bicucculline, which is mediated by NMDA receptors in low Mg2+ and by a combination of AMPA and NMDA receptors when Mg2+ is physiological.
bicuculline and Mg2+-free conditions are not sufficient to evoke polysynapses in the CA1 hippocampus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CA1 region is a complex network that is able to generate polysynaptic responses that are mediated by AMPARs and NMDARs.
the polysynapic responses are generated by local recurrent collatral of CA1 pyramids, which are mediated by AMPAR or NMDAR depending on the external Mg2+ concentration.
the polysynaptically driven events in the CA1 are mainly mediated by NMDA receptors, but in the presence of Mg2+ blockade they are mediated by AMPARs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polysynaptic activity can be evoked in the isolated CA 1 region of rat hippocampal slices and that this activity is mediated by glutamate receptors.
the CA1 region is a good model system to investigate polysynaptic responses.
we were able to record polysynaptic responses from CA1 pyramical cell dendrites in the presence of a low external concentration (0.3-1.3 mM) of Mg2+.
